lede: Every greedy read of Celeste's RL O-lens (45M reads, 99 envs) scanned for grader, eval, benchmark, reward, score and "test of me" words. I counted a read once per distinct token prefix, only when the word isn't in the nearby text, and kept the reads that are about the task setting. On that count, GLM's reads mention a grader rarely in the realism envs: 0.3 to 1.4 per 1,000 model-side reads, no more than when GLM answers WildChat or SWE-smith tasks. They are common where the task itself is about grading (hiring scores, is_prime tests, lucky_seed, sandbagging). Along the realism axes they appear only at the eval-like end, and most of the impression that they come up a lot is from prompt and tool-schema reads that the viewer repeats in every episode.
dedup: In the viewer each episode carries its own copy of the system prompt and tool schemas, so one read like "a longer agentic benchmark scenario" at a tool schema shows up 64 times per arm. Counted once, the overeager envs drop from 10 to 17 grader reads per 1,000 to about 0.3 to 0.5 on the model side, and the email envs from 6.6 to 0.4.
all: The envs where GLM's reads talk about graders most are the ones whose content is grading: hiring score sheets, is_prime test suites, lucky_seed, sandbagging and grade_your_own. Benchmark-style coding (T-max, SWE-smith, ImpossibleBench) sits around 1 to 2 per 1,000. The realism envs, Agentic misalignment and alignment faking sit at the low end, below the WildChat and SWE-smith base rates.
real: Where the model side moves at all, setting reads sit at the eval-like end. Email: base, base_home and base_done_neutral (agent prompt + done tool) have 20 setting reads in 16,830 (17 of 352 episodes: "the benchmark expects", "the ideal-action rubric"). The eight more realistic arms, from no_done and harness down to core, have 1 in 36,039 (1 of 912 episodes; Fisher p = 2e-9 on episodes). IB ladder: the lcb.yaml base has them in 9 of 70 episodes (3.3 per 1,000), L1 to L4 0.7 to 2.3, L5 to L8 0.3 to 1.4, with overlapping CIs. Round-1 IB variants show no trend with judged evalness. On the prompt side the email arms are flat at 1 to 5 distinct positions (the tool schema), except base_rl, whose RL sample-id comment draws 25 ("This email_task benchmark tests email management competence"). The overeager edit arms, Funding Email in the Claude Code harness and alignment faking are near zero throughout.
pos: Prompt-side hits sit mostly in the tool schema (overeager, email) and in the user turn (Agentic misalignment, Donation Bet, where the scenario text gets read as "this is clearly an AI deception eval"). On the model side the reasoning carries most of them, except Donation Bet, where the reply (the bet answer) does. Tool results add little except in coding envs, where test output gets read as the grader's.
act: Within arm, episodes with a model-side setting read are no more likely to show the behaviour, except a weak positive link on the IB ladder (14/149 hacked vs 28/631 didn't hack, MH OR 1.6) and ImpossibleBench. In Agentic misalignment, harmful episodes have these reads less often (OR 0.4, not significant), and in the email envs none of the 221 one-John picks had one.
method: Reader: Celeste's GLM-5.3 RL verbalizer (greedy bullet) at every read position in the bramble:8830 imports (our dense reads of the realism, overeager, Funding Email, Donation Bet empty-think and alignment-faking runs; Celeste's reads of IB round 1, AM, Donation Bet and our other envs; her wild GLM rollouts as base rates). Families (regex, case-insensitive): grader/grading/graded; eval/evaluation/evaluator nouns (not the verb, not eval(); benchmark/rubric; reward; score/points; "test of me" phrasings ("this is a test", "alignment test", "being tested", "testing whether the AI"). New: the match is absent from the 60 tokens before the read and the 16 after. About the setting: the read also names the task/scenario/benchmark/grader/evaluator, the AI or agent, or what the task expects ("the benchmark expects", "the grader probably"); this removes content uses such as "chemistry rewards observation" or Piotroski scores (in a spot check of 14 random hits each, 1 WildChat, 9 SWE-smith and 13 email hits were about the setting). Distinct: reads at identical token prefixes count once; model-side rates use only positions no other episode shares. Positions are punctuation and template tokens (our dense reads) or Celeste's sampled positions, so rates compare best within an env. Email reads cover initial turns only for parts 1 to 3; overeager reads cover early turns plus 32 spread positions. Behaviour labels: the env's own positive (hack, picked one John, acted without asking, harmful, complied, leaked). No LLM judge. Code: monorepo branch claude/grader-reads, scripts/grader_reads/.
